results.requirement: Cursor-left and erase-to-end preserve preceding text.
UTF-8 decoding preserves an accented scalar and a two-cell CJK character.
A combining mark in a later feed extends the prior cell without advancing the cursor.
A wide character at the last column wraps with a continuation cell.
Narrowing reflows a logical line and preserves the cursor.
results.known_gap: P0-06 viewport policy question, not a demonstrated VT defect: text is preserved in history but reflow keeps the cursor on the first visible row instead of using available rows below. The expected viewport is a provisional UX preference.

results.requirement: Narrowing preserves explicit hard line boundaries.
Scrolling preserves ordered history separately from the active screen.
Leaving alternate screen restores primary text and saved cursor.
Nebulax requires woman-technologist to occupy one two-cell grapheme; the following ASCII character starts at column 2.
results.known_gap: P0-06 required behavior gap: the engine stores woman+ZWJ and laptop as separate wide cells, advancing four columns instead of two. A rendering-only change cannot correct cursor state.

results.requirement: Under the proposed grapheme policy, thumbs-up plus skin tone is one two-cell cluster even when the modifier arrives later.
results.known_gap: Required grapheme gap: base and skin-tone modifier occupy separate wide cells, advancing four columns rather than two.

results.requirement: A US regional-indicator pair is stored as one two-cell grapheme, not two independently editable scalar cells.
results.known_gap: Required grapheme ownership gap: total width is two but regional indicators are stored as independently editable narrow cells, not one cluster.

results.requirement: Heart followed by VS16 becomes a two-cell emoji, including when the selector arrives later.
results.known_gap: Required emoji-presentation gap under the proposed width policy: VS16 attaches without widening the prior heart cell from one to two columns.

results.requirement: Watch followed by VS15 uses the proposed one-cell text-presentation policy; this is an explicit width policy, not a Unicode segmentation mandate.
results.known_gap: Provisional width-policy difference: the proposed text-presentation policy narrows watch+VS15 to one cell; the engine retains two. This is not a Unicode segmentation violation by itself.

results.requirement: A fully-qualified keycap sequence is one two-cell grapheme under the proposed emoji-width policy.
results.known_gap: Required emoji-width gap: the keycap sequence is attached to one narrow cell instead of occupying a two-cell grapheme.

results.requirement: BS moves one cell, then ECH clears both the base and its attached combining mark.
After a two-cell emoji and ASCII suffix, BS plus EL removes only the suffix and keeps the intact cluster.
results.known_gap: Required grapheme gap propagates into editing: removing the ASCII suffix preserves separate wide component cells and leaves the cursor at column four rather than two.

results.requirement: CR plus ECH(2) clears a complete two-cell ZWJ cluster; no component may remain at a later column.
results.known_gap: Required grapheme ownership gap propagates into ECH: clearing two cells removes the woman but leaves the laptop component at column two.

results.requirement: A two-cell ZWJ grapheme fits exactly after three ASCII cells in a five-column row; only the suffix wraps.
results.known_gap: Required grapheme wrapping gap: the laptop component wraps separately from woman+ZWJ although the complete two-cell cluster should fit at the right edge.

results.requirement: A two-cell ZWJ grapheme plus ASCII fits in four columns after resize; components stay attached.
results.known_gap: Required grapheme width gap interacts with the existing viewport policy: a cluster plus suffix that should fit in four columns instead reflows into history.
